questions.question: Compare nationalism’s role in developed and transitional societies. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• In developed societies, nationalism often serves symbolic unity - in transitional societies it
  • drives modernization and identity formation amid social, economic, and political
  • transformations following colonialism or authoritarian rule.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain Locke’s view of the constitutional state. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Locke viewed the constitutional state as one based on consent - limited government- and
  • separation of powers-ensuring protection of natural rights—life, liberty, and property—through
  • rule of law and accountable authority.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the difference between “internal” and “external” self-determination. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Internal self-determination concerns a group's autonomy within an existing state - external
  • self-determination refers to the right to form an independent state or secede from an existing
  • political entity.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is the meaning of "imagined community"? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• “Imagined community” means members of a nation feel connected despite never meeting
  • each other -nationalism creates this shared identity through media, symbols, and collective
  • imagination-explained by Benedict Anderson.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Why is primordialism criticized as ahistorical? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Primordialism is criticized as ahistorical-it treats nations and ethnic identities as natural and
  • timeless-ignoring their social construction and historical evolution through political, economic,
  • and cultural processes.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Define ethnic nationalism with examples. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Ethnic nationalism defines belonging through shared ancestry, culture, and language rather
  • than citizenship- example- German nationalism in the 19th century emphasized ethnic unity
  • over territorial boundaries or civic participation.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is the difference between nation-building and state-building? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Nation-building focuses on creating a shared national identity among citizens - state-
  • building emphasizes establishing effective political institutions and administrative structures -
  • ensure governance and public service delivery.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Examine the link between transnationalism and diasporic politics. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Transnationalism facilitates diasporic politics by enabling migrants to maintain political,
  • cultural, and economic ties with their homelands- influencing policy and identity across borders
  • through networks, technology, and global activism.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Apply the concept of “regional solidarity” to climate agreements. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Regional solidarity in climate agreements involves cooperation among neighbouring
  • countries to address shared environmental challenges - joint carbon reduction - disaster
  • management- promoting collective resilience and sustainable development.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyse globalisation’s role in language endangerment. / [CO4] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Globalisation endangers local languages by promoting dominant global tongues through
  • media, technology, and education- leading to cultural homogenization - the erosion of minority
  • linguistic traditions and local cultural identities.

questions.question: Compare ethno-symbolist and modernist interpretations of Zionism. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Ethno-symbolists view Zionism as rooted in enduring Jewish myths, symbols, and
  • collective memory- emphasizing cultural continuity - modernists interpret it as a product of
  • modernization and political mobilization responding to European nationalism and anti -
  • Semitism-these perspectives highlight cultural depth and modern political construction in
  • Zionist identity formation.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the major forms of nationalism. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Major forms of nationalism include civic or secular nationalism- emphasizing shared
  • political values and citizenship - ethnic nationalism, based on common ancestry and culture -
  • cultural nationalism- focused on heritage preservation- religious nationalism- integrating faith
  • with nationhood- economic nationalism- prioritizing domestic economic interests over global
  • integration and competition.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Compare protectionist practices of the US, EU, and China. / [CO4] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• U.S practices selective protectionism through tariffs and subsidies to safeguard key
  • industries-EU employs agricultural and environmental protectionism to defend regional
  • markets-China uses state-led protectionism via industrial policy, technology transfer controls -
  • export restrictions to strengthen domestic industries and maintain economic sovereignty in
  • global trade.
